claim: NPGL is a newly-identified neuropeptide that increased food intake and white adipose tissue (WAT) in rats.
source: We found that neurosecretory protein GL (NPGL), a newly-identified neuropeptide, increased food intake and white adipose tissue (WAT) in rats.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding of the study.

claim: NPGL-precursor gene overexpression in the hypothalamus caused increases in food intake, WAT, body mass, and circulating insulin when fed a high calorie diet.
source: NPGL-precursor gene overexpression in the hypothalamus caused increases in food intake, WAT, body mass, and circulating insulin when fed a high calorie diet.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding.

claim: Intracerebroventricular administration of NPGL induced de novo lipogenesis in WAT.
source: Intracerebroventricular administration of NPGL induced de novo lipogenesis in WAT, increased insulin, and it selectively induced carbohydrate intake.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding.

claim: Intracerebroventricular administration of NPGL increased insulin.
source: Intracerebroventricular administration of NPGL induced de novo lipogenesis in WAT, increased insulin, and it selectively induced carbohydrate intake.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding.

claim: Intracerebroventricular administration of NPGL selectively induced carbohydrate intake.
source: Intracerebroventricular administration of NPGL induced de novo lipogenesis in WAT, increased insulin, and it selectively induced carbohydrate intake.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding.

claim: Neutralizing antibody administration decreased the size of lipid droplets in WAT.
source: Neutralizing antibody administration decreased the size of lipid droplets in WAT.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding.

claim: Npgl mRNA expression was upregulated by fasting.
source: Npgl mRNA expression was upregulated by fasting and low insulin levels.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding.

claim: Npgl mRNA expression was upregulated by low insulin levels.
source: Npgl mRNA expression was upregulated by fasting and low insulin levels.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding.

claim: NPGL-producing cells were responsive to insulin.
source: Additionally, NPGL-producing cells were responsive to insulin.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding.

claim: NPGL is a novel neuronal regulator that drives food intake and fat deposition through de novo lipogenesis.
source: These results point to NPGL as a novel neuronal regulator that drives food intake and fat deposition through de novo lipogenesis and acts to maintain steady-state fat level in concert with insulin.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: NPGL acts to maintain steady-state fat level in concert with insulin.
source: These results point to NPGL as a novel neuronal regulator that drives food intake and fat deposition through de novo lipogenesis and acts to maintain steady-state fat level in concert with insulin.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: Dysregulation of NPGL may be a root cause of obesity.
source: Dysregulation of NPGL may be a root cause of obesity.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion stated in the abstract.

claim: Dysregulated energy balance can result in obesity and lead to serious health problems such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease.
source: Dysregulated energy balance can result in obesity and lead to serious health problems such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease (Steinberger and Daniels, 2003; Hill et al., 2012; Ahima and Lazar, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The arcuate nucleus (Arc) of the hypothalamus produces neuropeptide Y (NPY)/agouti-related peptide (AgRP) and α-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH), which are potent orexigenic and anorexigenic factors, respectively.
source: For instance, the arcuate nucleus (Arc) of the hypothalamus produces neuropeptide Y (NPY)/agouti-related peptide (AgRP) and α-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH), which are potent orexigenic and anorexigenic factors, respectively (Schwartz and Porte, 2005; Morton et al., 2006, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Leptin and insulin derived from peripheral tissues act on the hypothalamus to influence energy homeostasis.
source: In addition, leptin and insulin derived from peripheral tissues act on the hypothalamus to influence energy homeostasis (Baskin et al., 1999; Varela and Horvath, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A novel cDNA was identified in the chicken hypothalamus that encodes a precursor protein including a secretory protein of 80 amino acids.
source: As part of our search for novel neuropeptides and/or peptide hormone precursors in the hypothalamus, we identified a novel cDNA in the chicken hypothalamus and deduced a precursor protein including a secretory protein of 80 amino acids (Ukena et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: The small protein has Gly-Leu-NH2 at its C-terminal and was named neurosecretory protein GL (NPGL).
source: This small protein has Gly-Leu-NH2 at its C-terminal and was named neurosecretory protein GL (NPGL).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the naming and structure of NPGL.

claim: In chickens, subcutaneous infusion of NPGL increased body mass gain.
source: In chickens, subcutaneous infusion of NPGL increased body mass gain, suggesting that NPGL may be involved in growth processes, including energy homeostasis (Ukena et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Homologous Npgl genes were found in mammals, including human, rat, and mouse.
source: Subsequently, we found homologous Npgl genes in mammals, including human, rat, and mouse; the primary structure of NPGL is highly conserved among mammals and avian species (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to a figure showing sequence alignment.

claim: The primary structure of NPGL is highly conserved among mammals and avian species.
source: Subsequently, we found homologous Npgl genes in mammals, including human, rat, and mouse; the primary structure of NPGL is highly conserved among mammals and avian species (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to a figure showing sequence alignment.

claim: Rat NPGL assumes a circular structure.
source: Rat NPGL assumes a circular structure, although the mature structure has not been determined (Figure 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to Figure 1A showing the structure.

claim: NPGL could induce food intake in mice.
source: More recently, we found that NPGL could induce food intake in mice (Matsuura et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Npgl mRNA expression is high in the brain and testis of human and rat.
source: The results revealed that Npgl mRNA expression is high in the brain and testis of human and rat, but in mouse it only exhibits high expression in the brain (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to figures showing expression data.

claim: In mouse, Npgl mRNA only exhibits high expression in the brain.
source: The results revealed that Npgl mRNA expression is high in the brain and testis of human and rat, but in mouse it only exhibits high expression in the brain (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to figures showing expression data.

claim: Npgl mRNA was exclusively expressed in the mediobasal hypothalamus.
source: Npgl mRNA was exclusively expressed in the mediobasal hypothalamus (Figure 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to Figure 1B showing expression data.

claim: Western blot analysis demonstrated the presence of the mature form of NPGL in the hypothalamus.
source: Western blot analysis demonstrated the presence of the mature form of NPGL in the hypothalamus (Figure 1C).
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to Figure 1C showing western blot data.

claim: Both Npgl mRNA and its mature protein were localized to the lateroposterior division of the Arc (ArcLP) and the ventral tuberomammillary nucleus (VTM).
source: Histological analyses showed that both Npgl mRNA and its mature protein were localized to the lateroposterior division of the Arc (ArcLP) and the ventral tuberomammillary nucleus (VTM) (Figure 1D–I).
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to figures showing histological data.

claim: NPGL-immunoreactive fibers were observed only in the hypothalamus.
source: NPGL-immunoreactive fibers were observed only in the hypothalamus (Figure 1D and J).
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to figures showing immunohistochemistry data.

claim: NPGL's physiological role is mostly limited to regulation of the hypothalamus.
source: This latter result suggests that NPGL's physiological role is mostly limited to regulation of the hypothalamus.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that NPGL fibers are only in the hypothalamus.

claim: When rats were fed with high calorie diet, Npgl overexpression caused cumulative food intake to markedly increase.
